# Suman Debnath: the full Career Mode story

> Suman Debnath is a Senior Brand Marketing Manager in Pune, India, with 9+ years in brand and digital marketing. Since 2024 he has also built and shipped 26+ AI products on his own. This file is the complete text of his one-page résumé, Career Mode, in reading order.

This is the full text of https://hire.sumandebnath.houseofnamus.com/, where the story is told as a small pixel-art game: you scroll, and Suman walks through his career. Suman tells the story in the first person; MIGI, one of his AI agents, adds asides and logs the evidence. The short version, with a table of quotable facts, is https://hire.sumandebnath.houseofnamus.com/llms.txt. Last updated: 2026-11-18.

## Chapter 1 of 6: Kolkata

### Hi, I am Suman Debnath. (Today)

Senior Brand Marketing Manager in Pune, India. For 9+ years I have built brands, teams and launches, and since 2024 I have also shipped 26+ AI products on my own.

*MIGI: I log every skill he proves as you walk. Tell me what you are here for.*

### Here is what I bring, in four lines. (Today)

The rest of the walk is the evidence for each one.

Evidence (The short version):

- Brand: 8 years leading brand marketing, reporting to the Chairman and CEO.
- Team: 21 people across design, web and digital; 99% on time.
- Range: 20+ launches, 50+ websites, 1,000+ print and digital pieces.
- AI: 26+ products shipped solo, 46 agents, a model trained from scratch.

Skills shown: Brand strategy, Team leadership, Go-to-market, AI product building.

### I learned English late, and it taught me how persuasion works. (2009)

In 2009 I could not write one correct sentence. A tutor made me like the language first; two years later I earned a star mark.

*MIGI: I was built in 2026, so I am here as a hologram.*

Evidence (Kolkata, 2009):

- Went from no correct sentence to a star mark in English in two years.
- Kept the lesson: make people care before you ask them to remember.

Skills shown: Audience-first messaging, Persuasive writing.

### As a teenager I grew a Facebook page to 82,000+ followers, with no budget. (2013)

World of Lamborghini was a supercar page I ran from this bedroom.

*MIGI: He kept the screenshot of the 677,503. He did not believe it either.*

Evidence (My first audience):

- Grew the page to 82,000+ followers, all organic.
- One post reached 677,503 people.
- Ran the content calendar, community and analytics myself.

Skills shown: Social media growth, Content strategy, Community building.

### I taught myself SEO, ads, analytics and design to keep that page growing. (2014)

From YouTube tutorials, on a dial-up connection, years before anyone paid me to use them.

*MIGI: He was optimising watch time before he knew the phrase.*

Evidence (Self-taught):

- Learned SEO, Google Ads and Google Analytics on my own.
- Spent hundreds of hours in Photoshop, Premiere Pro and After Effects.
- Held viewers for 61.48% of one video's length, on average.

Skills shown: SEO, Google Ads, Google Analytics, Photoshop, Video editing, Motion graphics.

### In 2016 I left Kolkata to study marketing properly. (2016)

I had a degree in English literature, did not want to teach, and chose an MBA in Pune, where I knew nobody.

*MIGI: Distance to Pune: almost 2,000 km. He packed light.*

Evidence (Kolkata, 2016):

- Finished a BA in English (Honours), West Bengal State University, 2013–2016.
- Chose an MBA in Marketing over a second literature degree.

Skills shown: Written communication.

## Chapter 2 of 6: Pune

### Kolkata to Pune: east coast to west, almost 2,000 km. (2016)

The next eight years of my career happen at the other end of this road.

*MIGI: For the record, he did not walk it. This game only has a walk button.*

Evidence (The road to Pune):

- Moved across the country for an MBA in Marketing.
- Arrived in a city where I knew nobody.

Skills shown: Self-direction.

### MBA in Marketing at PIBM, with three internships. (2016)

I chose marketing because I had already been doing it for free since I was seventeen.

*MIGI: Finance: crossed out. HR: crossed out. You can watch it happen on the notice board.*

Evidence (Pune, 2016 to 2018):

- MBA in Marketing, Pune Institute of Business Management, 2016–2018.
- Interned at Nivea, Aamrit and Raman Byte.

Skills shown: Marketing strategy, Brand management.

### I built a complete agency brand, IllusionFX, before it had a single client. (2017)

On a 4 GB laptop in the college lab that rendered a few seconds at a time.

*MIGI: Clients: 0. Accuracy of the tagline, seven years later: 100%.*

Evidence (The computer lab):

- Made the logo, animated intro, brochures and plan myself.
- Wrote the tagline “Artificially Real”, years before I built AI products.

Skills shown: Brand identity, Collateral design.

### The one company I wanted cut me in the group discussion. (2017)

It was the exact brand and digital role I had waited two years for.

*MIGI: Watch the road. That rejection slip is still lying there.*

Evidence (November 2017):

- Cleared the written round.
- Did not get through the group discussion.

Skills shown: Resilience.

### So I showed the CEO my work, and he hired me on the spot. (2017)

My college director called the company's CEO and asked him to meet me.

*MIGI: Interviews held: 0. Job offers made: 1.*

Evidence (The same week):

- Showed my designs, websites, campaigns and an 80,000-follower page.
- Got the offer the same day, with no interview.

Skills shown: Portfolio-led pitching.

## Chapter 3 of 6: The first job

### In my first job I built a brand from nothing, alone, in ten months. (2018)

Branding and Digital Marketing Manager at CBS Ventures in Kerala, barely out of college.

*MIGI: Job titles: 1. Jobs actually done: at least 6.*

Evidence (Kerala, 2018):

- Built the positioning, identity, website and brand voice from zero.
- Ran design, video, SEO and paid campaigns myself.
- Interviewed candidates for the company as well.

Skills shown: 0-to-1 brand building, Paid campaigns, Hiring.

## Chapter 3 of 6: The gap

### Then four months between jobs, which I bridged with freelance work. (2018)

Two months in Kolkata and two in Bangalore, interviewing without success.

*MIGI: Mind the potholes. The bridge goes down one plank a month.*

Evidence (October 2018 to February 2019):

- Kept working through freelance design and digital projects.
- Kept interviewing until the next door opened.

Skills shown: Freelance client work.

## Chapter 4 of 6: The marketing floor

### Since 2019 I have led brand marketing at PIBM. (2019)

The business school where I did my MBA hired me back, and I report to its Chairman and its CEO.

*MIGI: Eight years of almost daily reporting. I counted.*

Evidence (PIBM, 2019 to today):

- Senior Brand Marketing Manager for a multi-brand higher-education group.
- Report directly to the Chairman and to the CEO, almost every working day.
- Own brand, web, print, paid media and launches across the group.

Skills shown: C-suite stakeholder management, Multi-brand management.

### I lead a 21-person team across design, web and digital. (2020)

Requests land from Admissions, Counselling, Sales and the academic heads at once.

*MIGI: He replaced the WhatsApp chasing. I checked.*

Evidence (The team):

- Set up written briefs, one owner per job and fixed revision rounds.
- Lead 12–15 direct reports and 6–9 more through shared projects.
- Delivered 99% of projects on time for six years.

Skills shown: Briefing systems, Project management, Cross-team coordination.

### I run 50+ websites and grew organic traffic by 40–50%. (2021)

Main sites, sister brands, programme microsites and landing pages: over 1,000 pages.

*MIGI: Five sites with payment gateways in one month. That one I double-checked.*

Evidence (Websites and search):

- Grew organic traffic 40–50% with content, technical SEO and page experience.
- Shipped five search-ready sites with live payment gateways in a month.
- Own the architecture, copy direction, design, QA and SEO.

Skills shown: Technical SEO, Website management, Information architecture.

### I have signed off 1,000+ print, outdoor and digital pieces. (2022)

Print does not take hotfixes: one typo on a press run costs lakhs.

*MIGI: ₹30–40 lakh is about $35,000 to $45,000 a year.*

Evidence (Print and production):

- Brochures, hoardings, newspaper ads, campus branding and video.
- Own a ₹30–40 lakh a year vendor budget, from rates to press run.
- Built a 200-page brochure in one day.

Skills shown: Print production, Vendor management, Budget ownership.

### I have run go-to-market for 20+ programme launches. (2023)

Each launch gets the full plan, from the brief to the lead form.

*MIGI: He plans the budget. The accounts desk holds the card.*

Evidence (Launches and paid media):

- Landing pages, SEO and lead campaigns on Google Ads and Meta Ads.
- Own the ad creative, campaign structure, remarketing and budget plan.
- Manage ₹40–60 lakh a year in marketing budgets.

Skills shown: Go-to-market, Meta Ads, Lead generation, Remarketing.

### I have built or repaired 150+ decks, and branded events in days. (2024)

Sales, pitch, product-showcase and counselling decks.

*MIGI: He still dislikes PowerPoint. The count keeps going up anyway.*

Evidence (Decks and events):

- Built a deck used in a live demo for a national education accreditor.
- Briefed and installed 50–100 branded pieces in three working days.

Skills shown: Presentation design, Event branding, Storytelling.

### I brought AI into my own team's work first. (2024)

Before building any product, I automated the dullest parts of our week, then trained the team to run it.

*MIGI: Those stairs lead down to where I come from.*

Evidence (AI in the team):

- Built an ad-creative pipeline that saves 2–3 hours a day.
- Cut 7–8 hours of photo retouching a week with a custom GPT.
- Clean thousands of lead rows daily; a site redesign went from weeks to hours.

Skills shown: Marketing automation, Custom GPTs, AI adoption and training.

## Chapter 5 of 6: The floors below

### In 2023 I taught myself to build with AI, end to end. (2023)

Prompts became context, context became workflows, workflows became agents, agents became products.

*MIGI: Steps in that chain: 5. Steps he skipped: 0.*

Evidence (Floor B1, 2023):

- Decide what to build, direct AI coding tools, review the output and ship.
- Work in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Next.js, Supabase, Vercel and n8n.

Skills shown: Prompt engineering, Context engineering, Agentic workflows.

### Since 2024 I have shipped 26+ AI products on my own. (2024)

Each one went from idea to live: strategy, design, build, launch and the marketing after.

*MIGI: Count verified: 26+, and not one is a demo. [See them all](https://sumandebnath.houseofnamus.com/projects)*

Evidence (Floor B2, 2024 to today):

- [AEGIS VAULT](https://aegisnote.houseofnamus.com/): encrypted notes whose server never sees your key.
- [That One Crawler](https://thatonecrawler.houseofnamus.com/): a free 53-check audit for search and AI.
- Over 200,000 lines of AI-assisted code across them.

Skills shown: AI product management, Product marketing, Shipping with AI tools.

### I built MIGI, a fleet of 46 AI agents that runs my admin. (2026)

They run my personal brand, job search, expenses, journal and uptime while I work.

*MIGI: This is where I was switched on. No longer a hologram. [Case study](https://sumandebnath.houseofnamus.com/agents/migi)*

Evidence (Floor B3, July 2026):

- Control it from a two-factor dashboard, a Telegram bot and an Android app.
- Guard it with 500+ automated checks.
- Run it for about $5 so far, where guides estimate $200 a month.

Skills shown: Multi-agent systems, LLM evaluation, AI cost control.

### I trained a language model from scratch, and fine-tuned one to run on a laptop. (2026)

Then I found a bug in my own scorer and corrected my published number.

*MIGI: 39.0% became 42.1%. The bug is lying in the corridor.*

Evidence (Floor B4, language models):

- [PentaCMD-47M](https://sumandebnath.houseofnamus.com/slms/pentacmd): 47M parameters, 299,000 pairs, about 87% exact match.
- [Qdex-1.5B](https://sumandebnath.houseofnamus.com/llms/qdex-1.5b): HumanEval 1.2% → 42.1%, on a 16 GB laptop.

Skills shown: Model training, QLoRA fine-tuning, Benchmarking.

### I build for places where a wrong answer is expensive. (2026)

Banking, money and other people's data.

*MIGI: The locked chest is ROASmind. Ask for early access*

Evidence (Floor B5, high stakes):

- [Banking Co-pilot](https://sumandebnath.houseofnamus.com/banking/rm-copilot): policy-cited answers, 38 security tests, 3 audits.
- ROASmind: an AI-native OS for Meta, Google and LinkedIn ads, in private testing.

Skills shown: Responsible AI, Security testing.

### Four rules I build by, each one from something that broke. (2026)

Each links to the notebook entry about the failure behind it.

*MIGI: Rule one is why I ask before I do anything that matters.*

Evidence (Floor B6, how I work):

- [No coding agent on autopilot](https://sumandebnath.houseofnamus.com/notebook/never-run-a-coding-agent-on-autopilot)

## Questions recruiters and clients ask

### Who is Suman Debnath?

Suman Debnath is a Senior Brand Marketing Manager at Pune Institute of Business Management in Pune, India, with 9+ years in brand and digital marketing. Since 2024 he has also built and shipped 26+ AI products on his own, including a 46-agent AI system and a language model he trained from scratch.

### Which Suman Debnath is this?

This is Suman Debnath the brand marketing leader and AI product builder from Pune and Kolkata, India: creator of the PentaCMD-47M language model, the MIGI agent fleet and ROASmind, and founder of House of Namus. He is not the cloud developer advocate, the power-systems researcher or the news-site web engineer who share the name.

### What roles is Suman Debnath looking for?

He is looking first for senior brand marketing leadership roles, and also for AI product marketing and AI product management roles. He is based in Pune, India, and is open to remote work and to relocation.

### What is Suman Debnath's marketing experience?

At Pune Institute of Business Management since March 2019 he has led a 21-person marketing, design and web team and reported directly to the Chairman and to the CEO. He has run go-to-market for 20+ programme launches, managed 50+ websites with over 1,000 pages, grown organic traffic by 40–50%, signed off 1,000+ print and digital pieces, and managed ₹40–60 lakh in annual marketing budgets.

### What AI products has Suman Debnath built?

His builds include MIGI, a fleet of 46 autonomous agents; PentaCMD-47M, a language model trained from scratch; Qdex-1.5B, a coding model that runs on a laptop; AEGIS VAULT, a zero-knowledge encrypted notepad; That One Crawler, a free SEO and AI-search audit; Slide Doctor, a deck audit; D-PE.ai, a prompt-engineering workspace; a banking co-pilot; and the games PixelVille and NUNO.

### Can I work with Suman Debnath on a project?

Yes. He takes on AI products, marketing automation and AI-visibility work. The quickest start is the free 15-minute AI consult, or an email to hire.sumandebnath@gmail.com.
